key_insight: GRPO did not reliably improve a small 4B–8B web agent over a strong supervised checkpoint; it only helped when the policy already had reachable headroom, and otherwise could be neutral or harmful.
engineering_relevance: For practical agent training, reward-optimized RL should be treated as a selective refinement step rather than a guaranteed upgrade, especially at small model scales and with moderate-to-high learning rates.
method: Controlled 18-run grid over learning rate, KL weight, seed, initialization, and clipping
Paired evaluation on text and Set-of-Marks screenshot observations with 25 eval seeds and 6 training seeds
Mechanistic follow-up using grafting and effective-rank analysis across 4B and 8B backbones
evidence_signal: Across the controlled grid, no setting credibly beat the strong supervised baseline on mastered tasks; on a reachable-reward control, the identical GRPO setup improved success by 22 points with an interval excluding zero.
watch_item: The failure is scale- and regime-dependent, so results may not transfer to larger backbones or to tasks with more latent headroom, and high learning rates can collapse performance.
paper_title: A Learning-Rate-Gated Failure of GRPO in a Small Language and Vision-Language Model Web Agent: A Controlled Null and Its Mechanism
